LOGIC INSTRUCTIONSE
The logic instructions consist of AND, OR, XOR, and NOT....
DISCUSSION
Let's start off with the AND instructions.
The AND function produces a "1" when both inputs are "1"...
If either or both inputs are "0" the result is "0".
The AND instruction of the 8086 microprocessor, ANDs two sets of data, either 8 bits or 16 bits, one bit at a time.
For example, ANDing these two sets of data produces 00101000.

One of the primary uses of the AND instruction is as a BIT MASK.
A bit mask is used to ensure certain bits in a byte or word are either set or reset...
The AND instruction is used to set certain bits to "0".....
Notice that the bit mask changes data bits 7 and 1 in the result.iall bits in the data are not changed except for bit 3.
Whenever the bit mask contains a "0", the AND instruction forces that bit position to "0".
Microprocessors have many AND instructions. Let's look at some typical ones.
AND REGISTER WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ANDs the contents of a register with the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
AND MEMORY WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ANDs the contents of memory with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
AND IMMEDIATE DATA WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ANDs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
AND AX, DATAA
AND IMMEDIATE DATA WITH REGISTER
This instruction ANDs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the register and places the result in the register.
AND X, DATA
AND REGISTER WITH REGISTER
This instruction ANDs the contents of one register with the contents of another register and place the result in the first register identified.

The next microprocessor logic instruction is the OR instruction.
The OR function produces a "1" when either or both inputs are "1".
If both inputs are "0", the result is "0".
The OR instruction in the 8086 microprocessor, ORs two sets of data, either 8 bits or 16 bits, one bit at a time.
For example, ORing these two sets of data produces 01111001.
What is the result of ORing these two sets of data in an 8086 microprocessor?ssor?
You did not OR the two sets of data correctly..............
TRY AGAIN!
The OR instruction is also primarily used as a bit mask....
The OR instruction is used to set certain bits to "1"......
Whenever the bit mask contains a "1", the OR instruction forces that bit position to a "1".
Microprocessors have many OR instructions. Let's look at some typical ones.
OR REGISTER WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ORs the contents of a register with the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
OR MEMORY WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ORs the contents of memory with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
OR IMMEDIATE DATA WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction ORs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
OR AX, DATAA
OR IMMEDIATE DATA WITH REGISTER
This instruction ORs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the register and places the result in the register.
OR REGISTER WITH REGISTER
This instruction ORs the contents of one register with the contents of another register and places the result in the first register identified.

The next 8086 logic instruction we will study is the XOR instruction....................
Recall that the XOR (or Exclusive OR) function produces a "1" when the inputs are opposite.
If both inputs are the same, the result is "0".
The XOR instruction in the 8086 microprocessor, XORs two sets of data, either 8 bits or 16 bits, one bit at a time.
For example, XORing these two sets of data in an 8086 microprocessor produces 00110110.
What is the result of XORing these two sets of data in an 8086 microprocessor?ssor?
You did not XOR the two sets of data correctly.............
TRY AGAIN!
The XOR instruction is used primarily for checking to see if data is the same or opposite.
If the data is the same and is XORed the result contains zero.
If the data is opposite and is XORed the result contains all ones.
If the data is not the same or opposite, the result contains 1's and 0's.
Microprocessors have many XOR instructions. Let's look at some typical ones.
XOR REGISTER WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction XORs the contents of a register with the accumulator and places the results in the accumulator.
XOR MEMORY WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction XORs the contents of memory with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
XOR IMMEDIATE DATA WITH ACCUMULATOR
This instruction XORs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the accumulator and places the result in the accumulator.
XOR AX, DATAA
XOR IMMEDIATE DATA WITH REGISTER
This instruction XORs the contents of the instruction code data with the contents of the register and places the result in the register.
XOR X, DATAA
XOR REGISTER WITH REGISTER
This instruction XORs the contents of one register with the contents of another register and places the result in the first register identified.
Which mnemonic identifies a XOR instruction between registers?

TRY AGAIN!
The last 8086 microprocessor logic insstruction we will examine is the NOT instruction.rlogic instruction for microprocessors is NOT.
The NOT or complement function inverts all bits............
The NOT instruction in a microprocessor NOTs 8 or 16 bits of data, one bit at a time.
For example, NOTing this data in an 8086 microprocessor produces 01010101.
What is the result of NOTing this data in an 8086 microprocessor?ssor?
You left the data as it was. You should have changed each 1 to a 0 and each 0 to a 1.
TRY AGAIN!
You only changed the 1s to 0s. You should have also changed all the 0s to 1s.
TRY AGAIN!
The NOT instruction is used primarily for taking the 1s and 2s complement of data.
The 1s complement is straight forward, you NOT the data....
The 2s complement requires taking the 1s complement and adding 1.
Microprocessors have many NOT instructions. Let's look at some typical ones.
NOT ACCUMULATOR
This instruction complements the accumulator.
NOT REGISTER
This instructions complement the contents of the identified register.
